standard_prerequisites: The formal completion X_{/T} of an algebraic space along a closed subset, and its functoriality under the modification f : X' to X which is an isomorphism over the complementary open
The faithful gluing lemma of the same chapter (equality of morphisms from agreement on the open and after completion)
The coequalizer construction in the pushouts section of Pushouts of Spaces, including essential constancy of the system X_n with value X
core_obligations: Uniqueness of the glued morphism from the faithful gluing lemma
Etale descent of the existence statement, reducing to X affine Noetherian
Equality of the two restrictions w' o pr_1 and w' o pr_2 over the fibre product square X'' using the faithful gluing lemma on X''

Construction of the glued morphism as the colimit of the coequalizer system: the maps w' amalgamated with w_n equalize s_n and t_n, descend to morphisms w^n : X_n to W compatible in n, and the system is essentially constant with value X
proof_roadmap: Fix the data w' and what-w satisfying the compatibility and prove uniqueness
Base change to an etale cover and assume X affine Noetherian
Prove a = b on X'' by the gluing lemma, so w' amalgamated with w_n equalizes the two projections of R_n
Descend along the coequalizer X_n, check compatibility of the system, and conclude by essential constancy
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is a bijection identifying morphisms from X with triples of morphisms from the modification X', the completion X_{/T}, and their common completion (source lines 6637-6717, label proposition-glue-modification). The solver must run an etale-descent reduction, prove the equality over the self fibre product by the gluing lemma, then build the glued morphism through infinitesimal neighbourhoods and the coequalizer system of the pushouts theory, closing with essential constancy; the assembly of the colimit system is a research-level argument, not a standard citation. Allowed background: the completion formalism and the cited pushouts lemmas, delivered as navigation pointers.
